definition: Techniques for reducing the number of tokens needed to represent a given piece of information in a model's context window, without losing essential meaning.
details: Context compression (through summarization, pruning less relevant content, or learned compression methods) helps manage the cost and latency implications of long context windows in production systems.
story: Picture a librarian organizing a million slips of paper so that any one of them can be found in a heartbeat. The examples a machine reads become the world it believes in. Better ingredients make a better meal, and the same is true here. Garbage in, garbage out — and the reverse: clean, representative data makes the model quietly brilliant. And that is Context Compression — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
